bio: Nalanda scholar turned yogi, Tilopa's disciple and source of the Six Yogas.

name: Marpa the Translator
bio: Tibetan householder-translator who brought Naropa's teachings to Tibet.

name: Milarepa
bio: Tibet's great yogi-poet, Marpa's disciple.

name: Gampopa
bio: Physician-monk who joined Milarepa's yoga with Kadampa monasticism.

name: Düsum Khyenpa, 1st Karmapa
bio: Gampopa's disciple and the first Karmapa, founder of Tsurphu.

name: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, 16th Karmapa
bio: Head of the Karma Kagyu who re-established the school in exile at Rumtek and brought it to the West.

image.artist: an employee of the Austrian Buddhist society

name: Ogyen Trinley Dorje, 17th Karmapa
bio: Recognised as the 17th Karmapa by the Dalai Lama and most Kagyu authorities; a rival candidate also exists.

name: Akong Tulku Rinpoche
bio: Co-founder and long-time abbot of Samye Ling in Scotland.

name: Chögyam Trungpa Rinpoche
bio: Tibetan teacher who co-founded Samye Ling, then founded Naropa University and Shambhala in North America.

name: Pema Chödrön
bio: American nun and author, a student of Chögyam Trungpa, resident teacher at Gampo Abbey.

name: Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche
bio: Eldest son of Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche and abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling in Boudha.

name: Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche)
bio: Eighth-century tantric master credited with establishing Buddhism in Tibet.

name: Gyokujun So-on Suzuki
bio: Soto priest who ordained Shunryu Suzuki and gave him dharma transmission.

name: Kishizawa Ian
bio: Soto scholar-teacher who further trained Shunryu Suzuki in Dogen's Shobogenzo.

name: Zentatsu Richard Baker
bio: Shunryu Suzuki's dharma heir and second abbot of San Francisco Zen Center.

name: Kōdō Sawaki
bio: Itinerant Soto master who stressed zazen alone ('homeless Kodo'); teacher of Kosho Uchiyama.

name: Muhō Nölke
bio: German-born former abbot of Antaiji.

name: Gudō Wafu Nishijima
bio: Japanese Zen teacher and Shobogenzo translator, Brad Warner's teacher.

image.artist: Permission granted by James M. Cohen, Attorney at Law

name: Hakuun Yasutani
bio: Founder of the Sanbo Kyodan, who taught Philip Kapleau and Taizan Maezumi.

name: Taizan Maezumi
bio: Founder of the Zen Center of Los Angeles; many American teachers are his heirs.

safety.summary: Maezumi admitted alcoholism and sexual relationships with students in 1983 (Betty Ford rehab); his own organization later published findings, reforms and an ongoing atonement process.

reports.outlet: Tricycle: American Zen Community in Crisis (Cushman)

name: Bernie Glassman
bio: Maezumi's first heir, founder of the Zen Peacemakers and teacher of Joan Halifax.

image.artist: Stephanie Young Merzel from Salt Lake City, Utah, USA

name: John Daido Loori
bio: Maezumi heir who founded Zen Mountain Monastery.

name: Philip Kapleau
bio: Author of The Three Pillars of Zen and founder of the Rochester Zen Center.

image.artist: No machine-readable author provided. Mind meal~commonswiki assumed

name: Eido Shimano
bio: Rinzai teacher who founded Dai Bosatsu Zendo; he resigned in 2010 after misconduct revelations.

name: Bodhidharma
bio: Legendary Indian monk honoured as the first patriarch of Chan.

name: Huineng
bio: Sixth Chan patriarch, figure of the Platform Sutra.

name: Thích Chân Thật
bio: Abbot of Tu Hieu Temple and Thich Nhat Hanh's root teacher.

name: Annamalai Swami
bio: Ramana Maharshi's attendant and builder who later taught self-enquiry from his small ashram.

name: Gangaji
bio: American teacher of self-enquiry who met Papaji in 1990.

name: Bhausaheb Maharaj
bio: Founder of the Inchegeri lineage at Inchgiri; teacher of Siddharameshwar.

name: Swami Ram (Kashmir)
bio: Kashmiri Shaiva master of the late nineteenth century, root of Lakshmanjoo's lineage.

name: Swami Mahatab Kak
bio: Disciple of Swami Ram and teacher of Swami Lakshmanjoo.

name: John Hughes
bio: Long-time student of Lakshmanjoo who recorded and publishes his teachings.

name: Alexis Sanderson
bio: Oxford Indologist of Shaiva tantra who read texts with Lakshmanjoo.

name: Lakṣmaṇagupta
bio: Pratyabhijna teacher of Abhinavagupta.

name: Kṣemarāja
bio: Abhinavagupta's leading disciple, author of the Pratyabhijnahrdayam.

name: Vasugupta
bio: Ninth-century sage to whom the Shiva Sutras were revealed.

name: Bhagawan Nityananda
bio: Avadhuta saint of Ganeshpuri and guru of Muktananda.

name: Swami Muktananda
bio: Founder of Siddha Yoga, who drew on Kashmir Shaiva texts.

name: Swami Chinmayananda
bio: Vedanta teacher who founded Chinmaya Mission and taught Swami Dayananda.

name: Swami Brahmananda
bio: Direct disciple of Ramakrishna and first president of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission.

name: Thomas Merton
bio: Trappist monk of Gethsemani and writer on contemplation and interfaith dialogue.

name: Thomas Keating
bio: Trappist abbot who helped develop Centering Prayer.

name: Brother Roger of Taizé
bio: Swiss founder of the ecumenical Taizé Community.

name: Bede Griffiths
bio: English Benedictine who led Shantivanam ashram and joined Christian and Hindu contemplation.

name: Swami Abhishiktananda (Henri Le Saux)
bio: French Benedictine who co-founded Shantivanam and was transformed by meeting Ramana.

name: Alexander von Rospatt
bio: UC Berkeley Buddhologist; co-chair of Christopher Wallis's dissertation committee.

name: Amitabh (Trika School of Tantra)
bio: Teacher of the Trika School of Tantra, which posts short teachings and guided meditations on Kashmir Shaivism; lineage not independently verified.

name: Guruji Amritananda Natha Saraswati
bio: Nuclear physicist (Dr Nishtala Prahlada Sastry, 23 years at TIFR Mumbai) who became a Śrī Vidyā guru and founded the Devipuram temple near Visakhapatnam, known for opening Śrī Vidyā initiation and Śrī Chakra worship to all.

name: André Padoux
bio: French diplomat turned CNRS scholar of tantric mantra and speech (Vāc); read Abhinavagupta with Lakshmanjoo in Srinagar in 1958–59.

name: Ben Williams
bio: Scholar-practitioner of Śaiva tantra and Abhinavagupta; frequent guest on yoga-studies podcasts.

name: Bettina Sharada Bäumer
bio: Austrian-born Indologist living in Varanasi; a student of Swami Lakshmanjoo who lectures on the Vijñāna Bhairava, Śiva Sūtras, Spanda and Netra Tantra and on Abhinavagupta's aesthetics.

name: Bjarne Wernicke-Olesen
bio: Danish scholar of Śākta and Kubjikā traditions.

name: Satguru Bodhinatha Veylanswami
bio: Head of Kauai's Hindu Monastery (Kauai Aadheenam) and publisher of Hinduism Today; successor of Sivaya Subramuniyaswami in the Nandinatha Sampradaya, teaching a monistic Śaiva Siddhānta.

name: Csaba Kiss
bio: Budapest (ELTE) Indologist; Oxford doctorate on the Matsyendrasaṃhitā, editor of Brahmayāmala volume II.

name: Daniel Odier
bio: French writer and teacher of Kashmiri Tantra (Spanda, Kālī practice, Tāṇḍava) and Chan; many uploads are in French, only English ones are kept.

name: Daniela Bevilacqua
bio: Ethnographer of Hindu ascetics on the Haṭha Yoga Project.

name: David Gordon White
bio: UCSB historian of religions (PhD Chicago 1988) known for The Alchemical Body, Kiss of the Yoginī and Sinister Yogis.

name: Dominic Goodall
bio: Sanskritist at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (head of its Pondicherry centre 2002–2011); editor of early Śaiva Siddhānta texts such as the Kiraṇavṛtti and the Niśvāsatattvasaṃhitā.

name: Douglas Brooks
bio: Professor of religion at the University of Rochester (PhD Harvard) and founder of the Rajanaka teaching, rooted in South Indian Śrī Vidyā as learned from his teacher Gopala Aiyar Sundaramoorthy.

name: Edwin Bryant
bio: Rutgers scholar of the Yoga Sūtras and Bhāgavata Purāṇa.

name: Elizabeth De Michelis
bio: Cambridge scholar of modern yoga (A History of Modern Yoga); supervised Mark Singleton.

name: Éric Baret
bio: French teacher in the line of Jean Klein who presents Kashmir Shaivism as a non-dual, body-based listening.

name: Gavin Flood
bio: Oxford scholar of Hinduism and comparative religion; author of The Tantric Body and studies of the Netra Tantra and Śaiva theology.

name: Gopala Aiyar Sundaramoorthy ("Appa")
bio: Sanskrit professor at Madurai-Kamaraj University and teacher of Douglas Brooks; source of the Rajanaka teaching.

name: Gorakhnāth (Gorakṣanātha)
bio: Founder-figure of the Nāth yogīs, credited with haṭha texts such as the Amaraugha.

name: Harunaga Isaacson
bio: Professor of Classical Indology at Hamburg, specialist in Indian Vajrayāna Buddhism and its links with tantric Śaivism.

name: Igor Kufayev
bio: Russian-born, Europe-based teacher whose darshans and courses draw heavily on Kashmir Shaivism (Trika, Krama, Spanda) and on kundalini as the process of awakening.

name: Jaideva Singh
bio: Indian scholar whose English translations of the Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam, Śiva Sūtras, Spanda Kārikās and Vijñāna Bhairava made Kashmir Shaivism widely readable; worked closely with Lakshmanjoo.

name: James Mallinson
bio: Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and leader of the Haṭha Yoga Project; edited the Khecarīvidyā, Dattātreyayogaśāstra and Amṛtasiddhi; also an initiated Rāmānandī mahant.

name: Jason Birch
bio: Historian of medieval yoga on the Haṭha Yoga Project; editor of the Amanaska, Amaraugha and Yogacintāmaṇi.

name: Judit Törzsök
bio: Professor of Śaiva Studies at the EPHE, Paris; works on early Śākta tantras such as the Siddhayogeśvarīmata and on yoginī cults.

name: Kavitha Chinnaiyan
bio: Cardiologist and teacher of Śrī Vidyā and Advaita (Svatantra Institute).

name: Lakulīśa
bio: Traditional founder of the Pāśupata ascetic order, the earliest named Śaiva movement (Atimārga).

name: Lilian Silburn
bio: French CNRS Indologist who studied Trika with Lakshmanjoo from 1949 and published French translations of the Vijñāna Bhairava, Śiva Sūtras and (with Padoux) the Tantrāloka.

name: Loriliai Biernacki
bio: Scholar of Hindu tantra (University of Colorado Boulder) writing on women in tantra, Abhinavagupta, wonder and new materialism.

name: Lorin Roche
bio: Meditation teacher known for The Radiance Sutras, a free poetic rendering of the Vijñāna Bhairava.

name: Louis Renou
bio: French Vedic scholar who directed Lilian Silburn's thesis and taught André Padoux Sanskrit.

name: Mark Dyczkowski
bio: English Indologist and sitarist who lived four decades in Varanasi; initiated by Lakshmanjoo in 1976; translator of the Spanda texts, the Manthānabhairava Tantra and the 11-volume Tantrāloka. Died in Varanasi on 2 February 2025. Since April 2026 his students Arjun Seernels and Brian Campbell lead the Anuttara Trika Kula Reading Circles.

name: Mark Singleton
bio: Scholar of modern and premodern yoga (Yoga Body, Roots of Yoga with Mallinson); senior researcher on the Haṭha Yoga Project.

name: Mary Reilly Nichols
bio: Yoga and meditation teacher formed in Siddha Yoga who teaches Kashmir Shaivism.

name: Matsyendranātha
bio: Legendary founder of the Kaula yoginī cult and first guru of the Nāth lineage.

name: Om Swami
bio: Indian monk and author who teaches mantra sādhana and Śrī Vidyā; many talks are in Hindi, so only English uploads were kept.

name: Paul Muller-Ortega
bio: Scholar of Indian religions (PhD, University of California) who taught at Michigan State and Rochester for 25 years, then founded Blue Throat Yoga (2006) to teach Neelakantha Meditation from the Śaiva–Śākta tradition of Kashmir.

name: Rajarshi Nandy
bio: Indian upāsaka of Bhairava, Kālī and Kāmākhyā who founded the Kamakhya Bhairava Upasaka Foundation (KBUF); speaks in English, sometimes mixed with Hindi, on Shākta sādhana.

name: Pandit Rajmani Tigunait
bio: Spiritual head of the Himalayan Institute and successor of Swami Rama; Sanskritist who teaches Śrī Vidyā, the Śrī Sūkta and tantric mantra practice.

name: Richard Gombrich
bio: Oxford Indologist and Buddhologist; supervised Mark Dyczkowski's doctorate.

name: Robert P. Goldman
bio: UC Berkeley Sanskritist; co-chair of Christopher Wallis's dissertation committee.

name: Sadhguru (Jaggi Vasudev)
bio: Founder of the Isha Foundation; consecrated the Linga Bhairavi goddess form at Coimbatore and teaches Bhairavi Sadhana as a devotional practice open to lay people.

name: Sally Kempton
bio: Journalist turned monastic in Swami Muktananda's Siddha Yoga (met Muktananda in 1974; initiated as Swami Durgananda in 1982); later an independent teacher of meditation, Kashmir Shaivism and goddess practice (Awakening Shakti, Meditation for the Love of It).

name: Seth Powell
bio: Historian of yoga and founder of the Yogic Studies platform and podcast.

name: Shaman Hatley
bio: Scholar of early tantric Śaivism and yoginī cults (UMass Boston); editor of the Brahmayāmala.

name: Shambhavi Sarasvati
bio: Spiritual director of Jaya Kula in Portland, Oregon, teaching Trika Shaivism alongside Tibetan Dzogchen; Anandamayi Ma is her root guru.

name: Satguru Sivaya Subramuniyaswami (Gurudeva)
bio: American-born founder of Kauai's Hindu Monastery and Himalayan Academy, initiated by Yogaswami of Jaffna; author of Dancing with Siva and Merging with Siva.

name: Somadeva Vasudeva
bio: Professor at Kyoto University; his Oxford doctorate edited the yoga chapters of the Mālinīvijayottaratantra; works on esoteric Śaiva yoga and Sanskrit poetics.

name: Somānanda
bio: Author of the Śivadṛṣṭi, first philosophical statement of non-dual Śaivism in Kashmir; teacher of Utpaladeva.

name: Sravana Borkataky-Varma
bio: Scholar of Śākta tantra in Assam and of women practitioners.

name: Sthaneshwar Timalsina
bio: Nepali-born scholar-practitioner (San Diego State University) who teaches Śākta and Śaiva tantra through his Vimarsha Foundation.

name: Swami Khecaranatha
bio: American teacher in the line of Swami Rudrananda (Rudi) who teaches Trika Shaivism and kundalini practice through his Heart of Consciousness community.

name: Swami Rama
bio: Founder of the Himalayan Institute and teacher of Pandit Rajmani Tigunait.

name: Swami Rudrananda (Rudi)
bio: American teacher of kundalini practice, root of Swami Khecaranatha's line.

name: Swami Shankarananda
bio: Disciple of Swami Muktananda who founded the Shiva Ashram near Melbourne; teaches Kashmir Shaivism and his own self-inquiry method, the Shiva Process.

name: Tilmann Vetter
bio: Leiden Indologist; supervised Harunaga Isaacson's doctorate.

name: Utpaladeva
bio: Author of the Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā, the founding text of the Recognition (Pratyabhijñā) school; student of Somānanda.

name: Yamajit
bio: Teacher at the Tridevi Chamunda Mandir who streams long satsangs on the twelve Kālīs of the Krama, the Mātṛkās, the 64 Yoginīs and Vijñāna Bhairava meditations.

name: Yogaswami of Jaffna
bio: Sri Lankan Tamil Śaiva sage, guru of Sivaya Subramuniyaswami.

name: Ajahn Brahmali
bio: Norwegian-born monk trained under Ajahn Brahm at Bodhinyana; teaches the early suttas and Vinaya closely, often co-teaching sutta courses with Bhante Sujato.

name: Bhante Sujato
bio: Australian monk ordained in the Ajahn Chah tradition; founder of Santi Forest Monastery and co-founder of SuttaCentral, where he has published free English translations of the four main Nikāyas.

name: Ajahn Hasapanna
bio: Monk of the Bodhinyana / BSWA community in Western Australia, a student of Ajahn Brahm.

name: Ajahn Ñāṇiko
bio: Senior monk at Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition; gives many of the monastery's evening and retreat talks.

name: Ajahn Karuṇadhammo
bio: American monk of the Ajahn Chah tradition and former abbot of Abhayagiri.

name: Ajahn Cunda
bio: Monk of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

name: Ajahn Sudhīro
bio: Monk of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

name: Ajahn Ahiṃsako
bio: Monk of Cittaviveka (Chithurst) Buddhist Monastery in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

name: Ajahn Karuniko
bio: Senior monk at Cittaviveka (Chithurst) in the Ajahn Chah tradition.

name: Ajahn Sona
bio: Canadian monk and co-founder of Birken Forest Monastery in British Columbia, in the Thai forest tradition; known for practical talks on jhāna and daily life.

name: Ajahn Anan
bio: Thai monk who ordained under Ajahn Chah in 1975 and founded Wat Marp Jan in Rayong; teaches weekly in Thai with English translation.

name: Ajahn Kalyano
bio: Australian monk, a long-time student and translator of Ajahn Anan; abbot of Buddha Bodhivana Monastery near Melbourne.

name: Ajahn Chandako
bio: American-born monk of the Ajahn Chah tradition; abbot of Vimutti Buddhist Monastery in New Zealand.

name: Sayadaw U Sīlānanda
bio: Burmese scholar-monk trained in the Mahasi tradition; founded the Theravada Buddhist Society of America and taught Abhidhamma and satipaṭṭhāna in California.

name: Sayadaw U Thuzana
bio: Burmese teacher in the Mahasi lineage who leads retreats at the Tathagata Meditation Center.

name: Sayadaw U Nandasiri
bio: Burmese teacher in the Mahasi lineage who leads retreats at the Tathagata Meditation Center.

name: Bhikkhu Anālayo
bio: German-born monk and scholar ordained in Sri Lanka; specialist in comparative study of the Pāli Nikāyas and Chinese Āgamas, and author of widely used books on satipaṭṭhāna.

name: Swami Pavitrananda
bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order who led the Vedanta Society of New York from 1951; heard here in archival recordings.

name: Swami Tathagatananda
bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and long-time head of the Vedanta Society of New York; heard here in archival recordings.

name: Swami Dhyanayogananda
bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of Southern California.

name: Swami Medhananda (Ayon Maharaj)
bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and philosopher (Ayon Maharaj), author of studies of Ramakrishna's and Vivekananda's philosophy.

name: Pravrajika Vrajaprana
bio: Nun of the Sarada Convent (Vedanta Society of Southern California) and author of books on Vedanta.

name: Pravrajika Krishnaprana
bio: Nun of the Sarada Convent, Vedanta Society of Southern California.

name: Swami Tyagananda
bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order, head of the Ramakrishna Vedanta Society of Boston and Hindu chaplain at Harvard and MIT.

name: Swami Chetanananda
bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order, minister of the Vedanta Society of St. Louis and author of histories of Ramakrishna's disciples.

name: Swami Shivarchanananda
bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order at the Vedanta Society of St. Louis.

name: Swami Ishatmananda
bio: Monk of the Ramakrishna Order and head of the Vivekananda Vedanta Society of Chicago.

name: Swami Tejomayananda
bio: Disciple of Swami Chinmayananda and former head of the Chinmaya Mission worldwide.

name: Swami Swaroopananda (Chinmaya Mission)
bio: Disciple of Swami Chinmayananda and current global head of the Chinmaya Mission.

name: Swamini Svatmavidyananda
bio: Traditional teacher of Vedānta in the line of Swami Dayananda Saraswati.

name: Swami Tattvavidananda
bio: Senior disciple of Swami Dayananda Saraswati teaching Vedānta and Sanskrit.

name: Swami Viditatmananda
bio: Senior disciple of Swami Dayananda Saraswati, long associated with the Arsha Vidya Gurukulam.

name: Radhanath Swami
bio: American-born Gaudiya Vaishnava teacher in ISKCON, a disciple of A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, and author of "The Journey Home".

name: Swami Niranjanananda Saraswati
bio: Successor of Swami Satyananda Saraswati and long-time head of the Bihar School of Yoga in Munger.

name: Swami Swaroopananda (Sivananda)
bio: Senior acharya of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres, a disciple of Swami Vishnudevananda.

name: Swami Sitaramananda
bio: Acharya of the Sivananda Yoga Farm in California, a disciple of Swami Vishnudevananda.

name: Swami Paramananda (Sivananda)
bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres (not the Ramakrishna-order Swami Paramananda, 1884–1940).

name: Swami Shambhudevananda
bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

name: Swami Brahmananda (Sivananda)
bio: Teacher of the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres (not the Ramakrishna-order Swami Brahmananda).

name: Ajahn Dtun
bio: Thai monk ordained at Wat Nong Pah Pong with Ajahn Chah as preceptor (1978); trained with Ajahn Piak and Ajahn Anan and founded Wat Boonyawad in Chonburi.

freeTexts.title: The Autobiography and Dhamma Teachings of Ajahn Dtun

name: Alexander Wynne
bio: British scholar of early Buddhism; Oxford DPhil under Richard Gombrich, author of "The Origin of Buddhist Meditation", and an editor of the Journal of the OCBS.

name: Rupert Gethin
bio: British scholar of the Nikāyas and Abhidhamma, emeritus professor at Bristol and president of the Pali Text Society; PhD at Manchester under Lance Cousins.

name: Steven Collins
bio: British scholar of Pāli Buddhism at Chicago, author of "Selfless Persons" and "Nirvana and Other Buddhist Felicities"; Oxford DPhil under Richard Gombrich.

name: Jeffery D. Long
bio: American scholar of Hindu and Jain traditions at Elizabethtown College, closely associated with the Vedanta Societies.

name: T. K. V. Desikachar
bio: Son and student of T. Krishnamacharya; founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in Chennai and taught yoga adapted to the individual.

name: Wendy Doniger
bio: American Indologist at the University of Chicago, translator of Sanskrit texts and author of "The Hindus: An Alternative History".

name: Nicholas Sutton
bio: Scholar of the Mahābhārata and Bhagavad Gītā who teaches the OCHS online courses.

name: Lance Cousins
bio: British scholar of Pāli and Abhidhamma (Manchester, Oxford) and samatha meditation teacher; supervised Rupert Gethin.

name: Paul Williams
bio: British scholar of Mahāyāna Buddhism at Bristol; taught Alexander Wynne and introduced Steven Collins to Gombrich.

name: Katukurunde Ñāṇananda
bio: Sri Lankan forest monk and author of "Concept and Reality" and the "Nibbāna – The Mind Stilled" sermons.

name: Balangoda Ānanda Maitreya
bio: Sri Lankan scholar-monk who was Bhikkhu Bodhi's preceptor.

name: Ajahn Piak
bio: Thai disciple of Ajahn Chah and abbot of Wat Pah Cittabhavana; Ajahn Dtun and Ajahn Anan trained alongside him.

name: Swami Tapovan Maharaj
bio: Himalayan Vedānta master at Uttarkashi; Swami Chinmayananda's teacher.

name: Swami Vishnudevananda
bio: Disciple of Swami Sivananda who founded the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

name: Swami Satyananda Saraswati
bio: Disciple of Swami Sivananda who founded the Bihar School of Yoga (1963).

name: T. Krishnamacharya
bio: South Indian yoga teacher whose students (Desikachar, Iyengar, Pattabhi Jois, Indra Devi) shaped modern postural yoga.

name: B. K. S. Iyengar
bio: Student and brother-in-law of Krishnamacharya; founder of Iyengar Yoga.

name: K. Pattabhi Jois
bio: Student of Krishnamacharya; founder of Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga in Mysore.

name: Chaitanya Mahāprabhu
bio: Bengali saint whose ecstatic Krishna devotion founded the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition.

name: Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī
bio: Founder of the Gaudiya Math and guru of A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada.

name: A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
bio: Founder of ISKCON (1966), who brought Gaudiya Vaishnavism to the West.

name: Daniel H. H. Ingalls
bio: Harvard Sanskritist; supervised Wendy Doniger's Harvard PhD.

name: Swami Paramarthananda
bio: Chennai-based disciple of Swami Dayananda, known for systematic English Vedānta classes (no official YouTube channel found).

name: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche
bio: Kagyu and Nyingma lama, founder of Nalandabodhi, who presents mind training and the "mindful gap" to modern audiences with humour and an interest in art and popular culture.

name: Ringu Tulku Rinpoche
bio: Karma Kagyu lama and scholar of the Rimé movement, former professor of Tibetan studies in Sikkim, who founded Bodhicharya and teaches in a light, accessible style.

name: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
bio: Bön lama trained at Menri under Lopön Tenzin Namdak, founder of Ligmincha International, who teaches Bön Dzogchen, dream yoga and the healing practices of sound and breath.

name: Valerie Forstman
bio: Associate Zen Master of the Sanbo Zen lineage and guiding teacher of Mountain Cloud Zen Center, first a student of Ruben Habito.

name: Chigan Roshi
bio: Rinzai Zen teacher with the Zen Studies Society who gives teisho on koan collections at Dai Bosatsu Zendo and New York Zendo.

name: Jeffrey Hopkins
bio: Scholar and translator of Gelug Madhyamaka and tantra, founder of the Tibetan Buddhist studies doctoral programme at the University of Virginia and the Dalai Lama's chief English interpreter 1979–89.

name: Lama Jampa Thaye
bio: British-born lama authorised in the Sakya and Karma Kagyu traditions by Karma Thinley Rinpoche, founder of the Dechen community and a scholar of Tibetan Buddhism.

name: Kwan Um School of Zen (various Zen Masters)
bio: The Kwan Um School of Zen, the international Korean Seon school founded by Zen Master Seung Sahn; the channel collects short talks by many of its Zen Masters.

name: Tendai Buddhist Institute (weekly dharma talks)
bio: Tendai Buddhist Institute in New York state, the American branch of Japanese Tendai; its weekly Wednesday talks cover Tiantai/Tendai doctrine and practice.

name: Foundation for Shingon Buddhism (classes and podcast)
bio: Foundation for Shingon Buddhism, which shares Shingon esoteric Buddhism, its texts and Koyasan culture in English.

name: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche
bio: Bhutanese Rimé lama of the Sakya and Nyingma lines, recognised as an incarnation of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo; filmmaker, author and founder of Siddhartha's Intent and Khyentse Foundation.

name: B. Alan Wallace
bio: American scholar-practitioner ordained by the Dalai Lama and trained by Geshe Rabten, later a Stanford PhD, who teaches shamatha and Dzogchen and argues for a "contemplative science" of mind.

name: Khentrul Rinpoche
bio: Shar Khentrul Jamphel Lodrö, a Jonang master trained in a non-sectarian (Rimé) way, who teaches Kalachakra and the shentong "other-emptiness" view through Dzokden.

name: Robert A. F. Thurman
bio: American scholar and translator, the first Westerner ordained a Tibetan Buddhist monk, Jey Tsong Khapa Professor at Columbia and co-founder of Tibet House US; died in June 2026.

name: Master Sheng Yen
bio: Taiwanese Chan master of the Linji and Caodong lines and founder of Dharma Drum Mountain, who revived Chan practice and taught in the West; his Great Dharma Drum TV series answers short questions.

name: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche
bio: Nyingma lama, son of Neten Chokling Rinpoche and former professor at Naropa, founder of Mangala Shri Bhuti, and teacher of Pema Chödrön.

name: Hokuto Daniel Diffin
bio: Rinzai Zen priest with the Zen Studies Society (Hokuto Osho) who gives Dharma talks on the Record of Linji.

name: Anne C. Klein (Lama Rigzin Drolma)
bio: Professor of Religious Studies at Rice University and, as Lama Rigzin Drolma, co-founder of Dawn Mountain in Houston, teaching Nyingma Dzogchen.

name: Thupten Jinpa
bio: Former Gelug monk with a Geshe Lharampa degree and a Cambridge PhD, principal English translator to the Dalai Lama since 1985, Tsongkhapa biographer and author of the Compassion Cultivation Training programme.

name: Jundo Cohen
bio: American Soto Zen priest living in Japan, Dharma heir of Gudo Wafu Nishijima and founder of the online Treeleaf Zendo.

name: Lama Tsultrim Allione
bio: American teacher, one of the first Western women ordained in Tibetan Buddhism (1970), founder of Tara Mandala and author of Women of Wisdom and Feeding Your Demons, a modern adaptation of Chöd.

name: Jan Chozen Bays
bio: Jan Chozen Bays, Dharma heir of Taizan Maezumi, paediatrician and co-abbot of Great Vow Zen Monastery in Oregon.

name: Rev. Meian Elbert
bio: Abbess of Shasta Abbey in the Order of Buddhist Contemplatives founded by Houn Jiyu-Kennett.

name: Jiryu Rutschman-Byler
bio: Soto Zen priest and former abbot of Green Gulch Farm, San Francisco Zen Center.

name: Anam Thubten
bio: Tibetan teacher trained in the Nyingma tradition who leads the Dharmata Foundation in California and teaches a direct, non-sectarian approach to awakening.

name: Phakchok Rinpoche
bio: Nyingma and Kagyu lineage holder, grandson of Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and founder of the Samye Institute.

name: Guo Gu
bio: Guo Gu (Jimmy Yu), Dharma heir of Master Sheng Yen and professor of religion at Florida State University, who teaches silent illumination and huatou at the Tallahassee Chan Center.

name: David Germano
bio: Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia, a historian of the Great Perfection (Dzogchen) and founder of the Tibetan and Himalayan Library and UVA's Contemplative Sciences Center.

name: Barry Magid
bio: Psychiatrist and Dharma heir of Charlotte Joko Beck who founded Ordinary Mind Zendo in New York.

name: Elizabeth Mattis Namgyel
bio: American teacher in the Nyingma line of Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche, author of The Power of an Open Question, who explores Madhyamaka "not knowing" in daily life.

name: Lama Lena
bio: American teacher (Yeshe Kaytup) of Dzogchen and Mahamudra, a long-time student of Wangdor Rinpoche, known for informal, precise "direct mind perception" teachings streamed from many cities.

name: Lama Shenpen Hookham
bio: British Kagyu and Nyingma teacher, Oxford DPhil on shentong buddha-nature, founder of the Awakened Heart Sangha.

name: Brother Phap Hai
bio: Plum Village monastic (Brother Pháp Hải), Dharma teacher in Thich Nhat Hanh's tradition.

name: Kokyo Henkel
bio: Soto Zen priest from the San Francisco Zen Center lineage, guiding teacher of Santa Cruz Zen Center, with a strong interest in buddha-nature texts.

name: Jetsunma Tenzin Palmo
bio: British-born Drukpa Kagyu nun who spent twelve years in a Himalayan cave and founded Dongyu Gatsal Ling nunnery.

name: Tulku Thondup Rinpoche
bio: Nyingma scholar trained at Dodrupchen monastery, former visiting scholar at Harvard, author of books on healing, the Longchen Nyingthig and the hidden treasure (terma) tradition.

name: Lama Rod Owens
bio: Black, queer Kagyu lama who completed a three-year retreat under Lama Norlha Rinpoche; teaches on anger, healing and collective liberation and leads Medicine Buddha practice online.

name: 34th Menri Trizin
bio: The 34th Menri Trizin, abbot of Menri Monastery in Dolanji and spiritual head of the Bön tradition, successor to Lungtok Tenpai Nyima (d. 2017).

name: Lama Willa Blythe Baker
bio: Kagyu lineage holder authorised after two three-year retreats, Harvard PhD (2013) and founder of Natural Dharma Fellowship and Wonderwell Mountain Refuge; teaches somatic mindfulness and Mahamudra.

name: Jan Willis
bio: Professor emerita of religion at Wesleyan and long-time student of Lama Thubten Yeshe, who writes on Tibetan hagiography, women and race in Buddhism.

name: Tenshin Reb Anderson
bio: Senior Dharma teacher at San Francisco Zen Center, ordained by Shunryu Suzuki, known for close readings of Dogen and the bodhisattva precepts.

name: Paul L. Swanson
bio: Scholar and translator of Tiantai at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture, translator of Zhiyi's Mohe zhiguan (Clear Serenity, Quiet Insight).

name: Donald S. Lopez Jr.
bio: Arthur E. Link Distinguished University Professor at Michigan, a historian of Tibetan Buddhism and of the Western reception of Buddhism.

name: Zen Master Dae Bong
bio: American Zen Master in Seung Sahn's Kwan Um School, guiding teacher at Hwagyesa International Zen Center in Seoul.

name: Duncan Ryūken Williams
bio: Soto Zen priest and professor at the University of Southern California, author of American Sutra on Japanese American Buddhists in wartime incarceration.

name: Alexander Berzin
bio: American scholar-translator who studied under Tsenzhab Serkong Rinpoche and the Dalai Lama in Dharamsala and created the Berzin Archives (now Study Buddhism), a large free library of Gelug and comparative teachings.

name: Brother Phap Huu
bio: Plum Village monastic (Brother Pháp Hữu), long-time attendant of Thich Nhat Hanh and abbot of Upper Hamlet.

name: Robert H. Sharf
bio: D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor of Buddhist Studies at UC Berkeley, a historian of Chan and Japanese Buddhism and a critic of "meditative experience" rhetoric.

name: Garchen Rinpoche
bio: Drikung Kagyu master who spent some twenty years in Chinese labour camps, where he trained under Khenpo Münsel; teaches love and compassion as the heart of Mahamudra through the Garchen Buddhist Institute in Arizona.

name: Sam van Schaik
bio: English Tibetologist at the British Library, author of Tibet: A History, Tibetan Zen and The Spirit of Zen, who works on Dunhuang manuscripts and early Dzogchen.

name: Brook Ziporyn
bio: Mircea Eliade Professor at the University of Chicago Divinity School, philosopher of Tiantai Buddhism and Zhuangzi.

name: Geoffrey Samuel
bio: Anthropologist of Tibetan religion, emeritus professor at Cardiff, author of Civilized Shamans and The Origins of Yoga and Tantra.

name: Bernard Faure
bio: French historian of Chan/Zen and esoteric Buddhism, emeritus at Columbia and Stanford, trained under Yanagida Seizan in Kyoto.

name: Jacob P. Dalton
bio: Khyentse Foundation Distinguished Professor of Tibetan Buddhism at UC Berkeley, a historian of tantric ritual, the Nyingma school and the Dunhuang manuscripts.

name: Brother Phap Linh
bio: Plum Village monastic (Brother Pháp Linh), Dharma teacher and musician in Thich Nhat Hanh's tradition.

name: Ruben Habito
bio: Filipino former Jesuit, Sanbo Zen teacher authorised in 1988 and founder of Maria Kannon Zen Center in Dallas.

name: José Ignacio Cabezón
bio: Dalai Lama Professor emeritus at UC Santa Barbara and former monk of Sera, who writes on Gelug and Nyingma philosophy, Sera monastery and Buddhist sexual ethics.

name: H.E. Asanga Vajra Rinpoche
bio: Sakya lama of the Phuntsok Phodrang line who teaches at Sakya Monastery of Tibetan Buddhism in Seattle.

name: Sakya Trizin (41st)
bio: Ngawang Kunga, 41st Sakya Trizin, head of the Sakya school for over five decades and now known as Sakya Trichen.

name: Sister Chan Duc (Annabel Laity)
bio: Sister Chân Đức (Annabel Laity), senior English-born Dharma teacher of Plum Village.

name: Zen Master Seung Sahn
bio: Korean Seon master of the Jogye order who founded the Kwan Um School of Zen and taught "only don't know".

name: Janet Gyatso
bio: Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard, a scholar of Tibetan visionary autobiography, medicine and gender.

name: Steven Heine
bio: Scholar of Dogen and Zen koans at Florida International University.

name: Taigen Dan Leighton
bio: Soto Zen priest and Dharma heir of Tenshin Reb Anderson, translator of Dogen and Hongzhi, guiding teacher of Ancient Dragon Zen Gate in Chicago.

name: Dosho Port
bio: Soto Zen teacher in the Dainin Katagiri line who hosts interviews with Zen teachers.

name: Kenneth K. Tanaka
bio: Shin Buddhist priest and scholar, professor emeritus at Musashino University, writing on Pure Land thought and Buddhism in America.

name: Dennis Hirota
bio: Scholar and translator of Shinran, head translator of the Collected Works of Shinran.

name: Peter N. Gregory
bio: Scholar of Chinese Buddhism, author of Tsung-mi and the Sinification of Buddhism, a central study of Huayan and Chan.

name: Richard K. Payne
bio: Scholar of Shingon ritual and tantric Buddhism, long-time dean of the Institute of Buddhist Studies in Berkeley.

name: John R. McRae
bio: Historian of early Chinese Chan, author of The Northern School and Seeing through Zen, trained by Stanley Weinstein and Yanagida Seizan.

name: Charles B. Jones
bio: Scholar of Chinese Pure Land and Taiwanese Buddhism at the Catholic University of America, author of Pure Land: History, Tradition, and Practice.

name: Karl Brunnhölzl
bio: German physician-turned-scholar and translator of Kagyu texts on Madhyamaka, Mahamudra and buddha-nature.

name: Khenpo Sodargye
bio: Nyingma scholar from Larung Gar in eastern Tibet who teaches widely in Chinese.

name: Sister Chan Khong
bio: Vietnamese nun and social worker, Thich Nhat Hanh's closest collaborator in relief work and co-founder of Plum Village.

name: Bodhin Kjolhede
bio: Abbot of the Rochester Zen Center and Dharma heir of Philip Kapleau.

name: Mark L. Blum
bio: Scholar of Japanese Pure Land Buddhism at UC Berkeley and translator of Honen and the Nirvana Sutra.

name: T. Griffith Foulk
bio: Scholar of Chan and Zen monastic institutions at Sarah Lawrence College and co-editor of the Soto Zen Text Project.

name: Laurence Freeman OSB
bio: Benedictine monk, student and successor of John Main, and director of the World Community for Christian Meditation.

name: Iain McGilchrist
bio: Psychiatrist and philosopher, author of The Master and His Emissary and The Matter with Things, on the hemispheres and the sacred.

name: Bernardo Kastrup
bio: Philosopher and computer engineer who argues for analytic idealism, the view that reality is fundamentally mental.

name: Arthur Green
bio: Scholar of Hasidism and neo-Hasidic theologian; doctorate under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis, founding dean of Hebrew College's rabbinical school.

name: Pir Zia Inayat Khan
bio: Head of the Inayatiyya since 2004, grandson of Hazrat Inayat Khan and founder of Suluk Academy; PhD in religion from Duke.

name: Omid Safi
bio: Duke University scholar of Islam who teaches Rumi, radical love and Sufi practice through his own courses and talks.

name: Shaykh Muhammad Hisham Kabbani
bio: Lebanese-American Naqshbandi-Haqqani shaykh, deputy and son-in-law of Shaykh Nazim, who founded the order's centres in North America.

name: Shaykh Dr. Nour Kabbani
bio: Naqshbandi teacher, son and successor of Shaykh Hisham Kabbani and grandson of Shaykh Nazim.

name: Baraka Blue
bio: Poet and teacher at the Rumi Center whose series Mirror of the Infinite teaches Rumi's Masnavi and the Sufi path of the heart.

name: Father Spyridon
bio: Orthodox priest who teaches the Jesus Prayer, repentance and the ascetic teaching of the Fathers in short talks.

name: Angela Puca
bio: Scholar of Western esotericism and magic who runs Angela's Symposium, an academic channel on theurgy, Hermetic magic and the grimoire tradition.

name: John Main OSB
bio: Irish Benedictine who recovered mantra meditation from John Cassian and the desert tradition; founding inspiration of the WCCM.

name: Moshe Idel
bio: Hebrew University scholar of Kabbalah who reframed the field around ecstatic Kabbalah and Abraham Abulafia.

name: Nimatullahi Sufi Order
bio: Official channel of the Nimatullahi order: illustrated classical Sufi teaching stories.

name: William Rowlandson
bio: Scholar of Borges, Swedenborg and the imaginal who supported the Kent MA in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

name: Angela Voss
bio: Scholar of Marsilio Ficino and the symbolic imagination who created the Kent and Canterbury MAs in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred with Geoffrey Cornelius.

name: Sarah Bachelard
bio: Australian Anglican priest and theologian teaching contemplative Christianity in the WCCM.

name: Becca Tarnas
bio: Scholar of archetypal cosmology, Jung and Tolkien, teaching on the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred diploma.

name: Peter Kingsley
bio: Scholar of the Presocratics who reads Parmenides and Empedocles as mystics and healers, and writes on Jung's Red Book.

name: Tom Cheetham
bio: Philosopher and poet, the leading English-language interpreter of Henry Corbin and of the imaginal in Corbin and Hillman.

name: Seyyed Hossein Nasr
bio: Iranian philosopher of Islam and the perennial philosophy, a leading Traditionalist author and teacher of Chittick.

name: Huston Smith
bio: American scholar of world religions, author of The World's Religions and Forgotten Truth.

name: James S. Cutsinger
bio: American scholar of the perennial philosophy and Eastern Orthodox spirituality, editor of Schuon.

name: James Finley
bio: Clinical psychologist and former Trappist novice under Thomas Merton; CAC faculty and host of Turning to the Mystics.

name: Louise Livingstone
bio: Scholar of the heart and Goethean enquiry, co-founder of the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred (2019).

name: William C. Chittick
bio: Scholar and translator of Ibn Arabi and Rumi; doctorate at Tehran University under Seyyed Hossein Nasr (1974).

name: Shaykh Nazim al-Haqqani
bio: Turkish Cypriot Grand Shaykh of the Naqshbandi-Haqqani order.

name: Geoffrey Cornelius
bio: Astrologer and scholar of divination, co-creator of the Kent and Canterbury MAs in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

name: Elliot R. Wolfson
bio: Scholar of Kabbalah and Jewish philosophy; doctorate under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis (1986).

name: Daniel C. Matt
bio: Scholar of Kabbalah and translator of the Pritzker Edition of the Zohar; studied under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis.

name: The Prometheus Trust
bio: UK charity founded in 1986 by Tim Addey and others to keep the Platonic tradition alive as a way of life; publisher of the Thomas Taylor Series.

name: Medina Tenour
bio: Teacher on Sufi women saints and nature contemplation at the Rumi Center.

name: Martin Lings
bio: English Sufi author and Shakespeare scholar, disciple of Frithjof Schuon and onetime assistant to René Guénon in Cairo.

name: Rowan Williams
bio: Theologian of Christian spirituality and former Archbishop of Canterbury (2002–2012).

name: Mary Attwood
bio: Art historian of the Renaissance imagination and director of the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

name: William Stoddart
bio: Scottish Traditionalist author on Sufism and the perennial philosophy.

name: Alireza Nurbakhsh
bio: Master of the Nimatullahi Sufi Order since 2008, succeeding his father Javad Nurbakhsh.

name: Cyprian Consiglio OSB Cam
bio: Camaldolese monk and musician teaching Christian meditation and interreligious contemplation.

name: Mirabai Starr
bio: Translator of the Spanish mystics and teacher of contemplative practice and grief.

name: Embassy of the Free Mind curators
bio: Curators of the Bibliotheca Philosophica Hermetica (Ritman Library) in Amsterdam, giving guided talks on its Hermetic and Böhme collections.

name: Arthur Versluis
bio: American scholar of Western esotericism and mysticism, founding editor of the journal Esoterica and author on Platonic mysticism and Gnosticism.

name: Patrick Curry
bio: Writer on enchantment, divination and ecology who taught on the Kent MA programme.

name: Wouter J. Hanegraaff
bio: Professor of History of Hermetic Philosophy and Related Currents at the University of Amsterdam and a founder of Western esotericism as an academic field.

name: Simon Wilson
bio: Canterbury Christ Church lecturer and course director of the MA in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred (2019–2021).

name: Frithjof Schuon
bio: Metaphysician of the transcendent unity of religions and founder of the Maryamiyya Sufi order.

name: Reza Shah-Kazemi
bio: Scholar of comparative mysticism and Islamic spirituality.

name: Jean-Louis Michon
bio: French scholar of Sufism and Islamic art.

name: Javad Nurbakhsh
bio: Psychiatrist and master of the Nimatullahi Sufi Order for 55 years (1953–2008).

name: Bernard McGinn
bio: University of Chicago historian of Christian mysticism, author of the multi-volume The Presence of God.

name: Christopher Titmuss
bio: British insight meditation teacher, former Thai monk, who co-founded Gaia House in 1983.

name: Christina Feldman
bio: Insight meditation teacher and author who co-founded Gaia House in 1983 and is now one of its patrons.

name: Stephen Batchelor
bio: British former Tibetan and Zen monk, author of secular Buddhist books such as "Buddhism Without Beliefs"; long linked with Gaia House.

name: Martine Batchelor
bio: French former Korean Seon nun and meditation teacher, a patron of Gaia House.

name: Lama Yeshe Losal Rinpoche
bio: Akong Rinpoche's younger brother; retreat master of Samye Ling from 1988 and its abbot since 1995.

name: Houn Jiyu-Kennett
bio: English Soto Zen roshi trained at Sojiji who founded Shasta Abbey (1970), Throssel Hole (1972) and the Order of Buddhist Contemplatives.

name: Daishin Morgan
bio: Disciple of Jiyu-Kennett and abbot of Throssel Hole Buddhist Abbey from 1982 to 2019.

name: Ajahn Khemadhammo
bio: English disciple of Ajahn Chah who founded the Forest Hermitage in Warwickshire and the Angulimala prison chaplaincy.

name: Sangharakshita
bio: English monk (Dennis Lingwood) who founded the Triratna Buddhist Community (formerly FWBO) in London in 1967.

name: Pramukh Swami Maharaj
bio: Guru and president of BAPS who inaugurated the Neasden mandir in 1995.

name: Kelsang Gyatso
bio: Tibetan lama who founded the New Kadampa Tradition and its mother centre at Conishead Priory, Cumbria.

name: Sophrony (Sakharov)
bio: Russian Orthodox elder, disciple and biographer of St Silouan the Athonite, who founded the monastery at Tolleshunt Knights in 1959.

name: Julian of Norwich
bio: English anchoress whose "Revelations of Divine Love" is the earliest surviving book in English known to be written by a woman.

name: George Fox
bio: English dissenter whose preaching from 1652 began the Religious Society of Friends (Quakers).

name: Bulent Rauf
bio: Turkish-born teacher around whom the Beshara School for the study of Ibn 'Arabi formed in the 1970s.

name: Ibn 'Arabi
bio: Andalusian Sufi master (1165-1240), "the greatest master", whose teaching on the unity of being shaped later Sufism.

name: Inayat Khan
bio: Indian musician and Sufi teacher who brought Sufism to the West, founding his order in London around 1914-1917.

name: Ross Nichols
bio: English poet and teacher who founded the Order of Bards, Ovates and Druids in 1964.

name: Gerald Gardner
bio: English civil servant who publicised the religion of Wicca from the 1950s.

name: Doreen Valiente
bio: English Wiccan priestess and poet, author of much of the Wiccan liturgy including the "Charge of the Goddess".

name: Dion Fortune
bio: British occultist (Violet Firth), founder of the Society (Fraternity) of the Inner Light and author of "The Mystical Qabalah".

name: Aleister Crowley
bio: English occultist, founder of Thelema, initiated in the Golden Dawn; owned Boleskine House.

name: Samuel Liddell MacGregor Mathers
bio: Co-founder of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn (1888) and translator of grimoires.

image.artist: The original uploader was Ihcoyc at English Wikipedia.

name: Emma Restall Orr
bio: English druid and writer who founded The Druid Network.

name: Philip Carr-Gomm
bio: Chosen Chief of OBOD from 1988 to 2020, pupil of Ross Nichols.

name: Kathy Jones
bio: Founder of the Glastonbury Goddess Temple and the Glastonbury Goddess Conference.

name: Cecil Williamson
bio: Founder of the Museum of Witchcraft, which settled in Boscastle in 1960.

name: Karl König
bio: Austrian paediatrician who founded the Camphill movement near Aberdeen in 1939-40.

name: Douglas Harding
bio: English philosopher whose "On Having No Head" launched the Headless Way.

name: Christmas Humphreys
bio: English barrister who founded the Buddhist Society in London in 1924.

name: John Crook
bio: British ethologist and Chan teacher, dharma heir of Sheng Yen, who founded the Western Chan Fellowship.

name: Francis of Assisi
bio: Troubadour turned friar of Assisi; married Lady Poverty and preached to birds, sultans and lepers alike.

name: Clare of Assisi
bio: First follower of Francis and founder of the Poor Clares; kept the privilege of poverty against popes and cardinals.

name: Bonaventure
bio: Franciscan minister general who joined Aristotle to the mystical ascent: the soul's journey into God in six illuminations.

name: Isaac Luria
bio: Mystic of Safed whose two years of teaching (1569–1572) remade Kabbalah around tzimtzum, shevirat ha-kelim and tikkun.

name: Hayyim Vital
bio: Foremost disciple of Luria, whose notebooks (Etz Chaim) preserve nearly all we have of the master's teaching.

name: Muinuddin Chishti
bio: Founder of the Chishti order in India, settled in Ajmer; remembered for service to the poor and love without distinction.

name: Nizamuddin Auliya
bio: Chishti master of Delhi whose assemblies joined princes and paupers; Amir Khusrau was his foremost disciple.

name: Amir Khusrau
bio: Poet, musician and disciple of Nizamuddin; credited with shaping qawwali and Hindavi poetry at the Chishti court of Delhi.

name: Abdul Qadir Gilani
bio: Hanbali preacher and mystic of Baghdad whose teaching founded the Qadiri order, the first widespread Sufi order.

name: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa
bio: Author of the Three Books of Occult Philosophy, the Renaissance summa joining natural, celestial and ceremonial magic.

name: John Dee
bio: Mathematician, astrologer and angel-conversationalist to Elizabeth I; his Enochian workings with Edward Kelley defined English learned magic.

name: Giordano Bruno
bio: Dominican turned Hermetic philosopher, burned in Rome in 1600; read the infinite universe as the unfolding of the divine mind.

name: Sayalay Dipankara
bio: Pa-Auk-trained Burmese nun (b. 1964); teaches the 40 kammatthana and vipassana worldwide; founder/abbess of the Brahma Vihari centres.

name: Ven. Ariyananda
bio: Senior meditation teacher of Na Uyana Monastery; gives the weekly English Dhamma talks and retreat interviews in the Pa-Auk system.

name: Uda Eriyagama Dhammajiva
bio: Abbot and chief preceptor of Meetirigala Nissarana Vanaya; scholar-practitioner of samatha and vipassana, author of 40+ publications.

name: Ven. Aggacitta
bio: Malaysian monk; founder and guiding teacher of Sasanarakkha Buddhist Sanctuary (Taiping), answering the shortage of trained local monks.

name: Bhikshuni Thubten Chodron
bio: American-born Tibetan Buddhist nun (bhikshuni); founder and abbess of Sravasti Abbey; author and imprison-chaplaincy pioneer.

name: Mata Amritanandamayi (Amma)
bio: Hugging saint of Kerala; heads the Mata Amritanandamayi Math and its worldwide charities; gives darshan to millions.

name: Raimundo Irineu Serra (Mestre Irineu)
bio: Rubber-tapper turned prophet of Acre; founded the Santo Daime doctrine in the 1930s, weaving Christianity, shamanism and African spirit ways around the Daime sacrament.

name: José Gabriel da Costa (Mestre Gabriel)
bio: Rubber-tapper of Rondônia; founded the União do Vegetal, teaching love of God and neighbour through the hoasca sacrament; doctrine affirmed by the US Supreme Court (2006).

name: Guru Nanak
bio: Founder of Sikhism (1469–1539); taught one God, honest work and shared food; composed the Japji Sahib.

name: Guru Gobind Singh
bio: Tenth Sikh Guru; founded the Khalsa (1699), closed the human Guruship in the Guru Granth Sahib.

name: Yogi Bhajan
bio: Brought Kundalini Yoga and Sikh Dharma to the West; founded the Espanola Mother Ashram (1970) and 3HO.

safety.summary: After December 2019 allegations (incl. Dyson's memoir), Yogi Bhajan's own organization commissioned An Olive Branch. Interviewing 299 people, the August 2020 report found it more likely than not that he engaged in sexual battery, sexual abuse, harassment and unethical conduct with 36 followers (1969–2004), with organizational enablers named. SSSC published it unedited.

reports.outlet: SSSC letter publishing the An Olive Branch report

name: Mahavira (Vardhamana)
bio: 24th tirthankara (traditional dates); reformer of the Jain path; taught ahimsa and anekantavada in the Gangetic plain.

name: Acharya Sushil Kumarji
bio: Jain monk who carried Mahavira's message West from 1975; founded Siddhachalam (1983), the only Jain tirth outside India; taught Arhum Yoga. No successor.

name: Laozi
bio: Traditional author of the Daodejing (6th c. BCE, traditional); root figure of philosophical and religious Taoism.

name: Baha'u'llah
bio: Founder of the Baha'i Faith (1817–1892); Kitab-i-Aqdas; taught the oneness of God, religion and humanity.

name: Abdu'l-Baha
bio: Son and appointed successor of Baha'u'llah (1844–1921); spread the Faith in the West; no clergy — elected order.

name: Sogyal Rinpoche
bio: Founder of Rigpa; Tibetan teacher (Nyingma tulku) whose books reached millions; stepped back in 2017 after misconduct allegations, died 2019.

safety.summary: After a July 2017 letter from eight former students, Rigpa commissioned an independent investigation (Lewis Silkin, led by Karen Baxter). The August 2018 report found, on the balance of probabilities, that some inner-circle students were subjected to serious physical, sexual and emotional abuse, and that senior Rigpa figures knew of some issues and failed to act. Not all allegations were upheld. Rigpa published the report and its boards' response.

reports.outlet: UK Charity Commission inquiry: Rigpa Fellowship

name: Sakyong Mipham Rinpoche
bio: Head of the Shambhala lineage (son of Chögyam Trungpa); stepped back from teaching duties in 2018 after misconduct claims and investigation.

name: Yogi Amrit Desai
bio: Founder of Kripalu (1972); resigned 1994 after admitting affairs; federal litigation followed; Kripalu restructured without him.

name: Rigdzin Kumaradza
bio: Dzogchen master; root guru of Longchenpa (Vima Nyingthig) and teacher of the 3rd Karmapa Rangjung Dorje.

name: Longchen Rabjam (Longchenpa)
bio: Systematiser of Dzogchen (Seven Treasuries); successor of Kumaradza; visions of Padmasambhava; re-revealed by Jigme Lingpa centuries later.

name: Jigme Lingpa
bio: Tertön whose Longchen Nyingtik visions made Longchenpa's Heart Essence the dominant Nyingma practice cycle.

name: Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu
bio: Hermit of Dzachuka; heart-disciple of Jigme Lingpa and root guru of Patrul (ngöndro 25 times).

name: Patrul Rinpoche
bio: Wandering yogi-scholar; Words of My Perfect Teacher; root-guru lineage Jigme Lingpa→Gyalwai Nyugu→Patrul→Mipham.

name: Jamgon Mipham (Ju Mipham)
bio: Prolific Nyingma scholar (30+ volumes); student of Patrul, Kongtrul and Khyentse Wangpo; teacher of Shechen Gyaltsap; named infant Dilgo Khyentse.

name: Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Thaye
bio: Rimé collector (Five Treasuries) with Khyentse Wangpo and Chokgyur Lingpa; teacher of Mipham; emanation-source of Kalu Rinpoche's line.

name: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo
bio: Tertön and Rimé founder with Kongtrul; root guru of Mipham; incarnation line continues (Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dilgo, Dzongsar).

name: Shechen Gyaltsap
bio: Mipham's heart-disciple; root guru of Dilgo Khyentse (enthroned him as Khyentse Wangpo's mind emanation).

name: Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö
bio: Activity emanation of Khyentse Wangpo; second root teacher of Dilgo Khyentse; taught all four schools to 80+ masters' heir.

name: Khenchen Jigme Phuntsok
bio: Founder of Larung Gar (world's largest Buddhist institute); root guru of Khenpo Sodargye; nonsectarian tertön.

name: 8th Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima
bio: Drukpa master of Khampagar (Tashi Jong); root guru of Jetsunma Tenzin Palmo (ordained her 1964).

name: Yonten Gyatso
bio: Jonang throne-holder; gave Dolpopa the complete Kalachakra/Dro transmission and named him heir (1326).

name: Huiguo
bio: Tang court master at Qinglong Monastery; poured the two-mandala transmission into Kukai in months (805); 7th Shingon patriarch.

name: Rendawa Zhonnu Lodro
bio: Sakya master of explanation; Tsongkhapa's foremost teacher (Pramanavarttika, Madhyamaka); later mutual instruction.

name: Phagmo Drupa Dorje Gyalpo
bio: Gampopa's chief disciple; teacher of Jigten Sumgon; the eight Kagyu branches divide from his seat.

name: Sachen Kunga Nyingpo
bio: Founder of Sakya (1073); first of the Five Forefathers; father and first teacher of Dragpa Gyaltsen.

name: Jetsun Dragpa Gyaltsen
bio: Third Sakya patriarch; son and student of Sachen; principal teacher of his nephew Sakya Pandita.

name: Sakya Pandita Kunga Gyaltsen
bio: Fourth Sakya forefather; epistemologist (Treasury of Reasoning); student of Dragpa Gyaltsen and Sakya Shri; negotiated Tibet's surrender (1244).

name: Tsangpa Gyare
bio: Founder of the Drukpa Kagyu (student of Ling Repa); 'Thunder-Dragon' line of the Himalayas.

name: Lingchen Repa Pema Dorje
bio: Drukpa yogi; teacher of Tsangpa Gyare (medium confidence — confirm before treating as settled).

name: Jigten Sumgon
bio: Founder of Drikung Kagyu (Drikung Thil 1179); chief disciple of Phagmo Drupa; Gongchig (Single Intention).

name: Niguma
bio: Wisdom dakini of Kashmir; sister of Naropa; source of the Shangpa transmission to Khyungpo Naljor.

name: Khyungpo Naljor
bio: Founder of Shangpa Kagyu; seven India journeys; received Niguma/Sukhasiddhi transmissions; one-to-one lineage begins.

name: Yizhin Norbu (Tsa Tsa Drubgen)
bio: Abbot of Tsa Tsa Monastery; gave Kalu Rinpoche the complete Shangpa cycle in closed retreat (1940s).

name: Khenchen Appey Rinpoche
bio: Sakya scholar (International Buddhist Academy founder); teacher of senior Sakya masters including Dzongsar Khyentse.

name: Rangjung Dorje (3rd Karmapa)
bio: 3rd Karmapa; student of Kumaradza (Vima Nyingthig); discussed view with Dolpopa at Tsurphu (1321).

name: Chenga Chokyi Gyalpo
bio: Drikung patriarch under whom Tsongkhapa studied Mahamudra and the Six Dharmas of Naropa.

name: Garab Dorje
bio: First human holder of Dzogchen (traditional account); taught Mañjushrimitra; lineage root of the mind section.

name: Mañjushrimitra
bio: Second Dzogchen holder (traditional); student of Garab Dorje, teacher of Shri Simha.

name: Shri Simha
bio: Third Dzogchen holder (traditional); student of Mañjushrimitra, teacher of Jñanasutra.

name: Jñanasutra
bio: Fourth Dzogchen holder (traditional); student of Shri Simha, teacher of Vimalamitra.

name: Vimalamitra
bio: Fifth Dzogchen holder (traditional); student of Jñanasutra; contemporary of Padmasambhava at Samye.

name: Saraha
bio: Mahasiddha of the doha songs; Mahamudra root figure; inspiration-line for Maitripa and Marpa's second transmission.

name: Maitripa (Advayavajra)
bio: Mahamudra master (1007–1085); Marpa's second guru after Naropa; Amanasikara cycle.

name: Aryadeva
bio: Nagarjuna's direct disciple; Four Hundred Verses; carried Madhyamaka to the south (and, traditionally, to Sri Lanka).

name: Ronald Davidson
bio: Fairfield historian of Indian esoteric Buddhism (Indian Esoteric Buddhism, Tibetan Renaissance); Vajrayana institutional history.

name: Jayaratha
bio: 13th-century Kashmir commentator whose Tantraloka-viveka unpacks Abhinavagupta's 37 chapters line by line.

name: Yogaraja
bio: Kashmir exegete; commentary on Abhinavagupta's Paramarthasara (Essence of the Highest Reality).

name: Bhaskararaya Makhin
bio: Sri Vidya polymath (1690–1785); Saubhagyabhaskara on the Lalita Sahasranama (1728), Setubandha (1748); initiated by Sivadatta Shukla at Surat.

name: Sadyojyoti
bio: Systematiser of Shaiva Siddhanta doctrine (c. 7th–9th c.); root figure of the dualist Shaiva schools.

name: Meykandar
bio: 13th-century Tamil philosopher; Sivajnanabodham (12 sutras); founded the Meykandar (Santana) Santana line via Paranjyoti's diksha.

name: Paranjyoti Munivar
bio: The sage 'descended from Kailash' who initiated the boy Meykandar on the street of Thiruvennainallur (traditional).

name: Tirumular
bio: Author of the Tirumantiram (3000 verses); among Nandinatha's eight disciples (traditional); Tamil Siddha root.

name: Nandinatha
bio: Legendary root guru of the Nandinatha Sampradaya; eight disciples incl. Tirumular (traditional).

name: Sukhasiddhi
bio: Wisdom dakini; student of Virupa; co-teacher (with Niguma) of Khyungpo Naljor's Shangpa transmission.

name: Yajnavalkya
bio: Upanishadic sage of the Brihadaranyaka; neti-neti dialogues with Maitreyi; debated by Gargi.

name: Uddalaka Aruni
bio: Father-teacher of Shvetaketu (Chandogya); 'Tat Tvam Asi' — thou art that.

name: Shvetaketu
bio: Uddalaka's son; received the nine homilies culminating in Tat Tvam Asi (Chandogya 6).

name: Gargi Vachaknavi
bio: Philosopher at Janaka's court; questioned Yajnavalkya on the woven-and-warped Brahman (Brihadaranyaka 3.6–3.8).

name: Maitreyi
bio: Yajnavalkya's wife-interlocutor; chose knowledge over wealth (Brihadaranyaka 2.4, 4.5).

name: Nachiketa
bio: Boy who questioned Death (Yama) and received the fire-doctrine and Self-knowledge (Katha Upanishad).

name: Satyakama Jabala
bio: Student of Haridrumata Gautama; truthfulness as qualification (Chandogya 4).

name: Vashistha
bio: Vedic seer (Rig Veda mandala 7); priest of Ikshvaku kings; Yoga-Vasishtha interlocutor.

name: Vishvamitra
bio: Seer of the Gayatri mantra (Rig Veda 3.62.10); rival-counterpart of Vashistha.

name: Vyasa (Krishna Dvaipayana)
bio: Traditional compiler of the Vedas and author of the Mahabharata; root figure of smriti.

name: Valmiki
bio: Traditional author of the Ramayana; 'first poet' (adikavi).

name: Agastya
bio: Vedic seer who carried the tradition south; Rig Vedic hymns + Tamil tradition root.

name: Kallaṭa
bio: Chief disciple of Vasugupta; received the Spanda-karika; bridge Vasugupta→Kashmir line.

name: Jalaluddin Rumi
bio: Persian poet-mystic (1207–1273); Divan and 25,000-verse Mathnawi; transformed by Shams (1244); order organized by son Sultan Walad.

name: Shams-i Tabrizi
bio: Wandering dervish whose 1244 Konya meeting transformed Rumi; Divan named for him; disappeared 1248 (traditional).

name: Baha al-Din Walad
bio: Rumi's father; Hanafi scholar-mystic of Balkh; family fled the Mongols to Konya; Rumi's first formation.

name: Sayyid Burhan al-Din
bio: Rumi's first Sufi master after his father (from 1232); nine years' training, forty-day retreats; directed his Aleppo studies.

name: Sultan Walad
bio: Rumi's son; first organizer of the Mevlevi order after Husam's death; Ibtidanama chronicler.

name: Sadr al-Din al-Qunawi
bio: Ibn Arabi's stepson and foremost disciple (ijaza for all works); systematized the school (wujūd, Perfect Man); teacher of Tilimsani, Jandi, Iraqi.

name: Gemistus Plethon
bio: Byzantine Platonist of Mistra; Bessarion's teacher; Laws manuscript burned as pagan; Council of Florence catalyst.

name: Basil Bessarion
bio: Plethon's student turned cardinal; carried Plato west (In calumniatorem Platonis); exegetical schemes fed Ficino.

name: Giovanni Pico della Mirandola
bio: Florentine Academy junior; Oration on the Dignity of Man (900 theses); Christian Kabbalah with Ficino's Platonism.

name: Augustine of Hippo
bio: Bishop of Hippo (354–430); read the Platonists (Enneads in Latin); Confessions/City of God; baptized Neoplatonism into Christianity.

name: John Scottus Eriugena
bio: 9th-century Irish scholar at Laon; translated Pseudo-Dionysius into Latin; Periphyseon; channeled theosis west.

name: Nicholas of Cusa
bio: Cardinal-philosopher (1401–1464); learned ignorance (De docta ignorantia); Eckhart and Proclus/Dionysius debts.

name: Parmenides
bio: Presocratic of Elea (c. 515–450 BCE); the Way of Truth; read by the tradition (and Peter Kingsley) as mystic, not logician.

name: Empedocles
bio: Sicilian healer-prophet (c. 495–435 BCE); four roots + Love/Strife; mystic-physician of the Western root.

name: Hsing Yun
bio: Founder of Fo Guang Shan (1967) and 200+ branch temples incl. Nan Tien; Humanistic Buddhism.

name: Swami Ramdev
bio: Yoga teacher and Patanjali Yogpeeth co-founder; mass yoga camps, Ayurveda institutions.

name: Shriram Sharma Acharya
bio: Founder of Shantikunj/AWGP (1971); Gayatri sadhana, Yug Nirman mission; 3500+ centres.

name: Swami Chidanand Saraswati
bio: President of Parmarth Niketan; Ganga Aarti host; interfaith water/environment work.

name: Ajahn Tong Sirimangalo
bio: Mahasi student (Rangoon 1957); abbot of Chom Tong 1991–2019; spread four-foundations vipassana to 11+ countries; Northern Vipassana dept.

name: Ajahn Martin Piyadhammo
bio: German-born Thai Forest monk (Maha Bua line); Wat Phu Kong Tong; blunt desanas answered from practitioner questions; 3 free books.

name: Ajahn Suphan
bio: Abbot of Wat Ram Poeng (Tapotaram); carries Ajahn Tong's Northern Insight 26-day curriculum.

name: Shihab al-Din Suhrawardi
bio: Founder of Illuminationism (1154–1191, Aleppo); Hikmat al-Ishraq; light metaphysics; executed.

name: Al-Ghazali
bio: Theologian-mystic (1058–1111); Revival of the Religious Sciences; studied under al-Juwayni; Sufi turn after crisis.

name: Mansur al-Hallaj
bio: Ecstatic martyr (858–922, Baghdad); 'I am the Truth'; associated with Junayd's circle.

name: Fariduddin Attar
bio: Nishapur poet-pharmacist (c. 1145–1221); Conference of the Birds, Memorial of the Saints.

name: Sanai
bio: Ghazna court poet turned mystic (d. c. 1131); Hadiqa (Walled Garden), first great Persian Sufi mathnawi.

name: Mulla Sadra
bio: Safavid philosopher (1571–1640); transcendent theosophy (al-hikmah al-muta'aliyah); student of Mir Damad.

name: Mir Damad
bio: Safavid philosopher-scientist (d. 1631); teacher of Mulla Sadra; School of Isfahan.

name: Al-Juwayni
bio: Asharite theologian of Nishapur (1028–1085); Ghazali's master; Shafi'i authority.

name: Junayd al-Baghdadi
bio: Baghdad master (d. 910); sober Sufism; Hallaj moved in his circle and was reproved by him.

name: Marinus of Neapolis
bio: Successor of Proclus as head of the Athenian school; wrote the Life of Proclus.

name: Thomas Aquinas
bio: Dominican theologian (1225–1274); Summa; baptized Aristotle through Augustine's Platonist legacy.

name: Chandrakirti
bio: 7th-century Madhyamaka commentator (Madhyamakavatara); Prasangika reading of Nagarjuna.

name: Shantideva
bio: 8th-century monk-scholar; Bodhicaryavatara (Way of the Bodhisattva); taught by Patrul/Mipham line ever after.

name: Asanga
bio: 4th-century systematizer (with brother Vasubandhu); Yogacara/Cittamatra; Abhidharmasamuccaya.

name: Vasubandhu
bio: Abhidharmakosha author; converted to Mahayana by brother Asanga (traditional); Yogacara co-founder.

name: Shantarakshita
bio: Nalanda abbot invited to Tibet (8th c.); founded Samye with Padmasambhava; teacher of Kamalashila.

name: Kamalashila
bio: Disciple of Shantarakshita; Samye debate victor (traditional); Stages of Meditation.

name: Jetsun Taranatha
bio: Jonang historian-yogi (1575–1634); Damchö Ling founder; Kālacakra systematizer after Dolpopa.

name: Yeshe Tsogyal
bio: Padmasambhava's consort-disciple (8th c., traditional); treasure revealer; Nyingma mother-line root.

name: Alara Kalama
bio: Meditation teacher of the Bodhisatta (formless attainments); left unsatisfied for Uddaka, then alone.

name: Uddaka Ramaputta
bio: Second teacher of the Bodhisatta (neither-perception-nor-non-perception); declined, went forth alone.

name: Arjun Seernels
bio: Close student of Mark Dyczkowski who co-leads the Anuttara Trika Kula online Reading Circles on the Tantrāloka (from April 2026).

name: Brian Campbell
bio: Student of Mark Dyczkowski and Sanskritist who co-leads the Anuttara Trika Kula Reading Circles; announced Dyczkowski’s death and the completed Tantrāloka translation on the INDOLOGY list.

name: Acharya Rameshwar Jha
bio: Varanasi pandit and Kashmir Śaiva teacher under whom the young Mark Dyczkowski studied.

name: Pandit Hemendra (Hemant) Nath Chakravarti
bio: Varanasi scholar, disciple of Gopinath Kaviraj, editor of a Tantrasāra translation; teacher of Mark Dyczkowski from 1971.

name: Gopinath Kaviraj
bio: Varanasi Sanskrit scholar and Tantric adept, disciple of Vishuddhananda and close to Anandamayi Ma.

name: Gurumayi Chidvilasananda
bio: Head of Siddha Yoga who inaugurated the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute in 1997.

name: Guru Yogi Matsyendranath Maharaj (Matsyeshvarnath)
bio: Russian-born Nāth yogi who lived long among Nāths in India, received full initiation and guru status, and teaches Nāth haṭha and tantric sādhanā internationally through nathas.org.

name: Yogi Lakshminath Maharaj
bio: Teacher in the nathas.org community who leads online courses on prāṇāyāma, meditation, āsana and Śiva Sūtra satsangs.

name: Yogi Allamanath
bio: Teacher in the nathas.org community (tea satsangs and talks on the NathaChannel).

name: Yogi Kamalnath
bio: Main pujari of the Gorakhnath Mandir, Gorakhpur; teacher of Yogi Mithileshnath.

name: Swami Sadatmananda Saraswati
bio: Chief ācārya of Arsha Vidya Gurukulam, Anaikatti, since 2014 and paramount trustee of Sruti Seva Trust; trained under Swami Brahmatmananda (Baroda, 1986) and taught at Arsha Vidya Kendra Bangalore 1994–2014.

name: Swami Brahmatmananda
bio: Student of Swami Dayananda who ran a three-year Vedānta course in Baroda (1986) attended by Swami Sadatmananda.

name: Swami Shankarananda Saraswati (Arsha Vidya)
bio: Disciple of Swami Dayananda teaching online Vedānta classes and retreats for AVG Anaikatti; ācārya of its Jan–Mar 2027 residential course. Distinct from Swami Shankarananda of Shiva Ashram (Kashmir Shaivism).

name: Swami Sakshatkrtananda Saraswati
bio: Senior Arsha Vidya teacher associated with Swami Dayananda Ashram, Rishikesh (listed in its About menu; ashram contact address sakshat1949@).

name: Mahamahopadhyaya Swamini Brahmaprakasananda Saraswati
bio: Senior disciple of Swami Dayananda and chief ācārya of Arsha Vijnana Gurukulam, Nagpur.

name: Swamini Vedarthananda Saraswati
bio: Faculty member at AVG Anaikatti who also looks after its temples.

name: Swamini Saradananda Saraswati
bio: Faculty member at AVG Anaikatti who also looks after its temples.

name: Swami Muktatmananda Saraswati
bio: Arsha Vidya teacher (Vedānta-sāra, Significance of OM series) at AVG Saylorsburg.

name: Swami Sachidananda (AVG)
bio: Arsha Vidya teacher and chanter at AVG Saylorsburg (Yoga of Objectivity series, satsangs).

name: Swami Advayatmananda
bio: Arsha Vidya teacher (Hastāmalakīyam course, guided meditations) at AVG Saylorsburg, 2025.

name: Swami Pratyagbodhananda
bio: Arsha Vidya teacher whose talks appear on the AVG channel.

name: Swamini Paraprajnananda
bio: Arsha Vidya teacher whose classes appear on the AVG channel.

name: Swami Atmaswarupananda
bio: Senior Divine Life Society monk who gives the morning meditation talks at the Christmas–New Year retreats, Sivananda Ashram.

name: Swami Krishnananda
bio: General secretary of the Divine Life Society for decades and prolific Vedānta lecturer (archival recordings).

name: KYM faculty (Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram)
bio: Collective teaching uploads of the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram: chanting, Dhanur-dhyāna sādhanā, prāṇa lecture series.

name: Geshe Lhakdor (Lobsang Jordhen)
bio: Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, former English translator to the Dalai Lama; teaches introductory Buddhism and Atiśa at LTWA.

name: Ven. Tenzin Gache
bio: FPMT teacher presenting Nāgārjuna’s Seventy Stanzas and Sixty Stanzas at Root Institute.

name: Ven. Tenzin Legtsok
bio: FPMT teacher ("Exploring the Mind Itself") at Root Institute.

name: Geshe Tenzin Zopa
bio: Gelug geshe teaching Atiśa’s Lamp for the Path and the Wheel of Sharp Weapons at Root Institute.

name: Guru Yogi Mithileshnath Maharaj
bio: Dharmanāth-panthī sadhu of Gorakhpur, student of Yogi Kamalnath and Yogi Dasharathnath, appointed head of the Nāth temple at Devi Patan in 2011; guru of Yogi Matsyendranath.

name: Swami (Sannyasi) Charanashrit Giri
bio: Founder-guru of Swara Yoga Peeth, Rishikesh; karma-sannyāsin of Paramahamsa Niranjanananda (Bihar School of Yoga), teaching the Śiva Svarodaya since 1993; titled Mahamandaleshwar in recent videos.
